items.title: Apple Has iPads Running macOS Internally, Says Gurman
items.snippet: Apple has iPads running macOS internally and has had them "for some time," according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman, although he says no work is currently being done to bring the Mac operating system to iPads. Speaking on his latest Power On podcast , Gurman said there is "no work being done to consumerize macOS on the iPad." Rather, Apple will continue to bring Mac features and apps like Final Cut to iPadOS piece by piece. Gurman also argued that per-operating-system EU regulation gives Apple an incentive to keep distinct systems for each device. Apple recently dismissed merging iPadOS and macOS. Here are the details. Wispr Flow this week launched Canto-2, its newest speech-to-text model, which the company says reduces transcription errors by 36% across 14 languages and by more than 15% in English compared to its predecessor, Canto-1. In practice, that means the average error rate dropped from 9.9% to 6.3% across the 14 languages, and from 3.2% to 2.7% in English, according to Wispr’s internal benchmarks. According to the company, teaching a model to recognize specific names and terms comes with a trade-off: the more it relies on that user-specific context, the more likely it is to insert those words even when they weren’t actually spoken. Wispr notes that Canto-2 strikes a better balance between context and accuracy, improving its ability to recognize user-specific terms without substantially increasing the frequency of incorrect substitutions: Canto-2 recovers hard names…

items.title: Apple tests extra widget space for the iPhone Duo Lock Screen
items.snippet: Apple is testing adding two more widgets to the iPhone Duo’s Lock Screen. The “complication column,” which lets Duo users choose from various widgets, is switched off for now, though. The experiment shows that Apple is still exploring ways to maximize use of screen space on the first-ever foldable iPhone. But it remains unclear if or when the customization tweak will go live. The first foldable iPhone, which hit stores a month ago, forced Apple to rethink the iOS user interface from the ground up. The result is a short Home Screen on the outer display, with familiar icons moved to the right, and a delightful animation as you unfold the device to reveal its wide inner screen. New multitasking and StandBy modes take advantage of the new form factor. For nearly two decades, the iPhone’s basic interface has revolved around a rectangular screen and a grid of apps. A foldable demands a different approach — and Apple continues to tweak the user experience. Currently, widgets on the iPhone Duo‘s Lock Screen sit along the right edge of the screen, at the top and bottom. Two default shortcuts…

items.title: 1Password has been hacked–passwords are safe, but admin data was accessed
items.snippet: Macworld 1Password is one of the most popular password managers, and one we’ve frequently recommended here at Macworld. Unfortunately, it has just suffered a major security incident . On November 19, a malicious attacker gained access to a 1Password employee’s corporate GitHub account. They used that to access the 1Password source code and get access to the company’s backend services, which holds the administrative data for customers. That’s stuff like customer names and email addresses, as well as public keys (but not private keys), account creation and sign-in times, and the like.
